newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Rights group urges probe on Ivorian student death.
newsitem.headline: Rights group urges probe on Ivorian student death.

text.p: Ivory Coast's LIDHO human rights league has called for an independent inquiry into the disputed death of a student which has raised tension at the West African nation's main university.

A LIDHO statement widely published by newspapers on Thursday also urged the government to stop treating the banned student union FESCI as an illegal group, arguing that this was unlawful and had contributed to campus tension.

But the government, in a statement after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, said that FESCI had been banned in 1991 following the murder of a student and anyone claiming to represent it was liable to face prosecution.

"Faced with the contradictory versions surrounding the death of the student Akpele A. Mercellin, the league asked the president of the republic and the government to set up an independent commission of inquiry," the statement said.
Student activists and the main opposition newspaper La Voie blamed the death on police brutality during a raid on a FESCI meeting at a residence hall in Abidjan's Abobo suburb on Sunday.
The government rejected this, noting the student had died the following evening.

Abidjan university was paralysed on Wednesday following a 72-hour strike call by FESCI over the death, grant arrears, lack of student accomodation and the jailing of three militants for two years on January 7 for inciting violence.
LIDHO said the 1991 decree scrapping FESCI carried no signature and that the government had itself since treated FESCI as a recognised organisation in a 1993 education debate.
